text.text_excerpt: In love with this gorgeous inn. The entire accomodations were fantastic! Monica is the best hostess! Each breakfast was tasty! Our room was romantic and comfotable! The cable car stops directly in front making it convenient to get around. My husband and i will be back to this special gem.

Room #7 is a great room. Kind bed, closest to the back patio and community fridge. They also have a little "work out" room near by equipped with an elliptical, yoga stuff and weights. The room is modern, spacious and very comfortable. Be aware that the sunlight is harsh in the morning so bring an eye mask if you're sensitive. Also, it is an old house so just be aware that the shower will take forever to heat up, but it will. The house itself is nice and in a good location outside of the craziness of French quarter craziness. This is an utter gem, if you want to dissolve into classical revival architecture this is the place. It is like stepping on to the set of Gone with the Wind. The building is decorated opulently with period pieces from the early 1900's, it was owned by a wealthy widow of a sheet metal baron. A lazy dog stretches out in the hall, nonplussed by the guests. The history of the place is fascinating and the rooms pull you in and tempt you to become the next Tennessee Williams or similar artistic geniuses from the South.
